report_title: Final commitment: certified aggregate-gate coefficient tightening
claim_class: same-coordinate identity bijection: 3 claims {integer forward, integer reverse, LP reverse} with full inverse pairing and per-coordinate obligations
headline: The reformulation never changes shape (48,417 binaries / 2,187 rows on both sides, 1,995,817 nonzeros): it rewrites 1,975 negative gate-control coefficients -|S| -> -M - total magnitude 1,666,313 -> 13,274 - each justified by a cover certificate over 82 unchanged packing rows. The claim layer is the pure same-coordinate identity (three copies of the 48,417-pair identity projection), yet proving it cost 190,770 proof steps / 23,271,589 linear terms / 635,985 obligations / 83,954,707 work and a 64,064,045-byte RPA, all built by a 149-line preparer whose entire arithmetic core is the hand-written SparseBuilder class that 35 sibling preparers import.
reformulation: Pure coefficient tightening with an explicit cover certificate: for each of 1,987 rows sum(x[j], j in S) - |S| y <= 0 the negative control coefficient is reduced to -M where M is certified by partitioning S over unchanged packing rows (80 unit assignment equalities + c80/c81 activation equalities, 82 sources total) plus individual binary upper bounds; 1,975 rows improved (M from 1 to 63, 808 with M=1), 12 unchanged, no variable, row, bound, integrality marker, objective coefficient or nonzero count altered.
claims: 3 claims, one shape {reverse,input_integers,output_integers,objective:'Equal',projection,inverse} (tools/prepare_test70.py:105-119, cases/test70/request.json). The two models have the identical 48,417-variable / 2,187-row shape, so all three projections are the literal identity map and all three are byte-identical: .[0].projection[0:3] = [[0,0],[1,1],[2,2]], last pair [48416,48416].

'inverse' is a cross-claim index, not a flag: claim 0 (forward, integer) declares inverse 1 and claim 1 (reverse, integer) declares inverse 0, so they are mutual inverses; claim 2 (reverse, input_integers=false) declares inverse null (tools/prepare_test70.py:120-122).

Obligations by claim 244,273 / 244,273 / 147,439 (cases/test70/preparation.json:35-39) = 3 x 48,417 bound+integrality checks + 2,187 rows + 1 'Exact' objective + 48,417 projection 'Exact', plus 48,417 inverse 'Exact' in the two claims whose inverse is not null; 635,985 total (cases/test70/README.md:9).

Row obligations: in the forward claim the 1,975 edited gates discharge as local binary Cases steps (kernel statistics branches=1975) and the other 212 by direct refs to unchanged source rows; the reverse claim re-proves each source gate row from the target row plus the nonnegative multiplier (|S|-M) on the control's VarLower (tools/prepare_test70.py:107-118).

Claim 2 is objective-preserving LP inclusion: 'objective-preserving inclusion of the target continuous relaxation into the source relaxation', explicitly with no strict global LP containment claim (cases/test70/README.md:5). Kernel receipt: VERIFIED, work 83,954,707, peak_live_facts 190,770, linear_terms 23,271,589, execute 2.909 s, proof.rpx 61,393,184 B (cases/test70/preparation.json:88, cases/test70/README.md:9).
proof_encoding: 'RPA 2\n' + compact json of {claims,blocks} (tools/prepare_test70.py:130-132); each block is {'steps':[...],'end':{'Return':{'map':[48,417 identity expressions],'checks':[...]}}}.

Only two rules are emitted: Lin (the forward block's 190,770 steps, counts.forward_steps at cases/test70/preparation.json:33) and 1,975 local cases splits, each {'steps':child_steps,'end':{'Witness':ref}} over a VarInt control; everything else is a bare ref {'VarLower'},{'VarUpper'},{'VarInt'},{'RowEq'},{'RowUpper'},{'Local'} or the literal string 'Exact' (tools/prepare_test70.py:32-42, 105-119).

Each edited gate gets three derivations: an unconditional Lin bound (restricted packing supports + individual VarUpper terms = M), then the conditional row via the cases split (tools/prepare_test70.py:96-103).

Restricted packing bounds are ordinary Lin facts: the gate support is partitioned among the audit's cover rows, and each restriction cancels the non-support coordinates of a previously proved containing support using shared 64-coordinate chunk facts (tools/prepare_test70.py:75-95) - 7,052 restricted bounds, 262,213 cache entries, no new trusted rule.

Ids and facts live in shared mutable state: one counter list is threaded through every fork (tools/prepare_test88.py:19-23) and branch builders see the parent's facts through ChainMap({},parent.facts) (tools/prepare_test70.py:36-39).
agent_manual_work: Parsed the whole 100,426,160-byte / 2,093,812-line MPS with exact Fraction/Decimal in eval cells (sections NAME,ROWS,COLUMNS,RHS,BOUNDS,ENDATA; one INTORG/INTEND pair; 48,417 UP records; no RANGES/OBJSENSE) - digest eval 'Parsing exact sparse model'.

Hand-rolled the complete row classification behind the finding: 160 unit assignment equalities, 1,987 gates sum(S)-|S|y<=0 with binary control outside S, 13 activation equalities, 27 other rows; senses 173 E / 2,012 L / 2 G - digest eval 'Classifying exact row structures'.

Wrote the greedy cover construction with Python sets/frozensets over 82 packing sources (M ranged 1..63) and a separate verification pass over every certificate by incidence domination - digest evals 'Constructing exact gate coefficient certificates' and 'Verifying complete tightening scope'.

Rewrote the MPS with a hand-written field-width-preserving rewriter (regex spans over COLUMNS records) and emitted the 576,099-byte audit.json with schema 'exact-gate-cover-v1' (packing_sources + per-change row/control/old/new/cover_rows/individual_upper_bounds) - digest eval 'Writing single committed reformulation'.

Wrote a second independent parser + verifier (output/verify.py, 6,606 B) doing a line-by-line whitelist diff of both artifact files, plus 30,498 finite gate-equivalence checks; it recorded both SHA-256 digests - digest section 6 and eval 'Independently auditing committed artifact'.

:105-124 the three-claim loop (identity projection, per-coordinate checks, positional inverse wiring) and :137-146 the four-mutation harness that targets proof steps by position and term count.
friction: No construction API exists, so the corpus's builder core is one Python class in a preparer: 35 sibling preparers import SparseBuilder from prepare_test70 (grep -rl 'from prepare_test70 import.*SparseBuilder' tools/ = 35, e.g. tools/prepare_test10.py:14, tools/prepare_test31.py:9, tools/prepare_test8.py, tools/complete_test83.py:10).

The first generator never finished: interrupted at 402 s / 1,377,536 KiB RSS / exit 130 while emitting 42,216,226 referenced packing terms from 234,331 packing nonzeros (cases/test70/preparation.naive-interrupted.json:25,33,36).

Artifact cost is repetition, not mathematics: 64,064,045 bytes of RPA for 1,975 changed coefficients, of which restriction derivations contribute 7,371,020 parent terms and 6,150,027 cancellation terms (cases/test70/preparation.json:28-31); the naive route referenced 18,244,585 cancellation refs (cases/test70/shape_measurements.json:3).

Failure attribution and claim repetition: the four mutations are located by step position and term count (tools/prepare_test70.py:137-146) so their receipts name no obligation ('INVALID obligation mismatch: expected Le; obligation 96916'), and the 1,967,189-byte request is three byte-identical 48,417-pair identity projections with no compact way to say 'same coordinates'.

notes: SparseBuilder's real interface (reconstructed from tools/prepare_test70.py:14-30 and tools/prepare_test88.py:18-43). Inherited constructor: SparseBuilder(model, counter=None, facts=None, assumptions=None) where model is the parsed model dict {vars,rows,var_index,row_index,objective}; counter is a one-element mutable list [next_id] shared by every fork (else a fresh [0]); facts is a {id:(kind,expr)} dict copied at construction; assumptions is the list of enclosing branch expressions. Overridden lin(kind, terms, expected=None, constant=0) -> ref. Preconditions: kind in {Eq,Le,Int}; Eq requires constant==0, Le requires constant<=0, Int requires an integral constant; each term (ref,c) requires, by the referenced fact's kind, Eq->any multiplier, Le->kind=='Le' and c>=0, Int->kind=='Int' and c integral. Arithmetic: exact int/Fraction accumulator (total, coefficient dict) with an integer fast path so integral multipliers and coefficients never touch Fraction; no per-term copy of the supports (this is the documented reason the class exists). expected, when given, must equal the whole residual exactly. Error behaviour: every violation is a bare AssertionError - the per-term kind/multiplier preconditions, and one explicit message 'exact sparse residual mismatch' carrying only (constant, expected constant, len(support), len(expected support)), i.e. no offending term, rule or model location. Side effects: allocates an id from the shared counter and appends {'Lin':{'id','kind','constant','terms'}} to self.steps, recording ('kind',expr) in self.facts. Forking: branches are built by re-instantiating SparseBuilder(model, counter, assumptions=[...assumption]) and rebinding child.facts=ChainMap({}, parent.facts) (tools/prepare_test70.py:36-39), which is how a 190,770-entry fact map is shared without copying it per branch. Measured import fan-out: 35 files under tools/ import SparseBuilder from prepare_test70 (none of them test70's own three preparers).
